accepts.because: ask whether this actor may do this thing on this resource; the edge that carries it MUST promote the caller to context.requester, or the answer is requester_unknown
spend a grant: perform one operation the broker already said yes to; same promotion, because a grant belongs to somebody

emits.because: the verdict on a request -- granted, allowed (a check_only request: a yes with no grant behind it), denied with a reason_code, or pending; a handle and never a credential
the outcome of spending a grant, ok or denied plus a reason_code
the one call that leaves for the connector, addressed from the grant and from nothing else
a lane failed; which cell inside produced it is not the caller's business, and a parent that drains nothing loses every refusal

description.purpose: Scope marker of the access hive: the capability broker behind its own path. THE HIVE IS THE ADDRESS -- `params.ports` is empty, so no edge reaches a cell in here and a caller names the hive plus a lane on hop.route. Fourteen internal edges; the seven that are neither a door nor an exit exist for one reason -- a code cell has no cell.db, so the state of a multi-read lane rides in the hop keys these edges promote to context and comes back on the store's answer. The store round trip IS the cell's memory. TWO edges reach `./vault` (GH #421, reversing GH #307): `./invoke` asks on the `avault` lane and the answer comes back on the promoted context, exactly like the store round trip. What travels back is a SEALED BOX addressed to an ephemeral key the requester minted -- never a plaintext credential.
description.use_when: Once per member or per org level that owns credentials. Instantiate with add_nodes and wire the lanes in the SAME mutation, at the HIVE path. Both inbound lanes MUST promote the caller to `context.requester`: a grant without an edge-borne requester is a grant issued to whoever asked loudest (R-AC-1).
description.not_in_scope: No model of any kind -- every verdict in this hive is a comparison. No PLAINTEXT credential on the wire either: `./vault` holds them, and what leaves it is a ciphertext under a key only the requester holds for that one call (GH #421). `cred_refs` stays the CATALOGUE of names, and it is the catalogue the grant reads its `cred_ref` out of. And no enforcement of its own monopoly: that exactly one edge reaches the connector is a fact about the topology a parent draws, not a rule the substrate applies (see README, `The honest limit`).
description.contract_in: Two lanes, both at the hive path. in_request -- an access.request tool_call turn: may this actor do this. in_invoke -- an access.invoke tool_call turn: spend a grant. Older wirings named ./policy and ./invoke directly and declared them as `ports`; those are cell names, not lanes, and they moved the boundary one step instead of drawing it.
description.contract_out: Four lanes, all out of the hive path. grant -- the verdict. ack -- the outcome of an invocation. connect -- the one call for the connector, addressed from the grant. error -- any lane failed, and the parent MUST drain it.
